agree.reason: This reader remembers the refunds and has already given to the ambulance fund, and is likely to pledge: the draft takes on the old failure head-on, shows that $36,000 is already committed, and promises that every pledge comes back if the goal isn't met.

honest.reason: Every figure checks out, but two claims go further than the facts allow: "far cheaper to run" has no operating-cost figures behind it, and "We can reopen it by Thanksgiving" states a plan as a certainty.

works_the_facts.reason: The draft correctly works out $49,000 still to raise and makes the strongest comparison available, only $2,000 more than the last campaign actually raised, though it could also have put the target in reader terms, such as roughly $7.50 per resident.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is described accurately (the cinema stays dark and the nearest screen is 38 miles away), but the cost of that 76-mile round trip, or what the town has lost since 2022, is left for the reader to work out.

qualification.reason: The all-or-nothing condition names a date, an amount and a consequence, but the warning that the roof could cost up to 15% more gives no dollar figure and doesn't say who covers the shortfall or what happens to the project if it occurs.

objections.reason: The draft answers the refund worry directly, but for a reader stretched by other giving this month it offers only "pledge what you can", with no suggested amounts and nothing on why the pledge matters now.

fit.reason: This is a clear, signed campaign pitch of about 330 words, under the 350-word limit.
